_doc: WFACT 3.0 evaluation registry (Factory Completion Plan Step 7; Blueprint §14 'the direct successor to 2.0's 78-check registry'). Versioned data, read and validated by src/evalRegistry.ts; every entry is a check with an ID, category, severity, mode (automated or model-judged), runner, stage, what it proves, its 2.0 source, the model it uses (null = no model), a passing fixture and a deliberately broken fixture. Runners: text = deterministic HTML/site-file checks (packages/verification, every entry point); rendered = headless Chromium suite (packages/rendered-qa/src/rendered.ts); review = screenshot reviewer model; evaluator = independent evaluator model; attack = system attack run on demand and in CI, not per page. Severity: blocker and major fail the gate; minor (text runner only) fails as advisory (WARN, audited, not sent to the builder on its own). Stage: preview = every build; launch = launch-candidate checks that need the production domain (N/A at preview, reason recorded). Fixture paths are repo-relative: a .html file is one page; a directory is a site (pages = its .html files except 404.html unless 'pages' is given); {test, name} points at the committed test that holds the fixture. 'isolated': the broken fixture fails this check and no other check of its runner/stage. Order is the builder's fix order. Change any entry = bump version.

fixtureContext._doc: Context every text fixture runs with unless the fixture overrides it. Facts come from the SYNTHETIC Summit Line brief.

notCovered: Everything in sourceInventory.missing: the 78 registry checks and the 50 audit items cannot be ported item by item from this repo.
Auth bypass, session attacks and rate-limit bypass (2.0's three permanent NOT COVERED items) remain not covered; the client sites have no login, and the Cockpit's auth is Supabase's.
Upload attacks and the Owner's Key round trip / design lock: there is no Owner's Key or upload path in 3.0 yet.
Forms submitted for real and e-commerce checkout: built sites have no form handler yet (the form posts nowhere by design until a handler exists).
Real devices, Safari / iOS Safari, a mid-tier Android phone, throttled real networks and the 'site usable if JavaScript fails' check: Chromium on the runner only.
Dependency and history scans for client site builds (npm audit, gitleaks with history) run on this repo in CI, not on each built site.

Video budgets, the Experience Charter ('living canvas', scroll-owned moment, one world) and Arabic/RTL: no current builder emits video or RTL; the Charter is judged only by the screenshot reviewer's rules.

Launch-stage checks (canonical, og:image, sitemap, robots.txt, llms.txt, 404) need the production domain and run only with stage 'launch'; nothing calls that stage automatically yet because the factory never launches (human-gated), and today's starters fail them (see the Step 7 report).
Model-judged checks (render.design-review, evaluator) are proven against mocks in CI; their live behaviour was measured on 2026-10-01 (reviewer) and in Step 4B runs, not on every commit.
Agent 37 hermes-agent's underlying model is not disclosed by the gateway; the cross-model rule treats it as its own family (config/evaluator.json) on the gateway's self-description.
WebRTC and other non-HTTP egress from the QA browser are not separately filtered (the browser is launched behind a refusing proxy and every non-site request is aborted; WebRTC is not proxied).
